topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the final lecture and states what students should learn about cancer treatments.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how local treatment can remove or destroy tumors and how chemotherapy supports those interventions.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: This material examines how conventional cytotoxic drugs kill cells and how their clinical usefulness is constrained by toxicity and resistance.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how blocking required hormonal signals can selectively restrain breast and prostate cancer growth.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how missing cell cycle checkpoint proteins create vulnerabilities that treatments can exploit.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how inhibiting an additional DNA repair mechanism selectively kills cancer cells already deficient in BRCA-mediated repair.

topics.label: Oncogene-directed therapy and kinase inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics develop the strategy of targeting oncogenic drivers through kinase inhibition and explain why its effectiveness is limited by tumor adaptation.

topics.label: Antibody-directed targeting of cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how antibodies recognizing cancer cell surface proteins can direct therapeutic effects toward those cells.

topics.label: Immune surveillance and checkpoint blockade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine whether endogenous immunity recognizes cancer and how checkpoint blockade can strengthen that response.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells against cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe engineered approaches that give T cells targeted access to cancer cells rather than relying on their existing antigen recognition.

topics.label: Treatment challenges and biomarker-guided care
topics.groupedBecause: This material examines how patient selection and treatment monitoring can improve care despite cancer heterogeneity and therapeutic limitations.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends and prevention
topics.groupedBecause: This material evaluates improving cancer outcomes in light of changes in prevention and early detection.

topics.label: Future treatment priorities and ethical decisions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider how to pursue better cancer care when promising innovations must be weighed against established treatment benefits and patient quality of life.
